project_overview: This Vue.js application appears to manage exam and fee-related processes, utilizing multiple Vue components for different pages and functionalities. The application’s structure suggests a tiered approach, with components like ApplicationServices and defaultLayout potentially serving as foundational layers. The high number of components and routes indicates a relatively complex application requiring careful attention to maintainability and scalability. The project's architecture seems focused on providing user-facing interfaces for various exam-related tasks.

layers.description: User interface components responsible for rendering views and handling user interactions.
Low-level components or services supporting the presentation layer. This layer's existence is inferred from routes pointing to it and potential dependencies.

macro_trends.title: Potential UI Logic Leakage
macro_trends.description: Several Vue files (ExamFormSubmission, iLikeCourses, SelectedApplicationService) are labeled with 'Logic' issue types, potentially indicating the presence of business logic embedded within presentation components. This violates the principle of separation of concerns and can lead to maintenance challenges.

macro_trends.title: Route Driven Development
macro_trends.description: The architecture heavily relies on Router navigation, particularly for routing user interactions to ResultPage and other key components.  This could lead to tightly coupled components and difficulty refactoring or altering the application flow.

key_workflows.name: Exam Result Flow
key_workflows.description: This workflow begins with a user interacting with components like ExamFormSubmission, FeeDetails, HallTicketPage, and ultimately navigates to ResultPage.  This highlights a critical path within the application and requires careful optimization of data retrieval and rendering within ResultPage.
